label: Copy-phase input k (recall position >= 3), strongest when the next output is f
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter steps), and almost only when the fed-back input is the letter k (96% of activation mass; f and p add a small tail). It is almost silent at recall_idx 0-2, so it is concentrated at recall positions >= 3 and in longer sequences (L=9 holds 48% of mass). Magnitude depends strongly on the token output at that step: out_tok f has 13.9x lift and gives the top activations (k followed by f in the original, e.g. 0 e 2 k f ...), and p/r/z/n/h follow. Precision is low: only about 16% of copy-phase k inputs at recall_idx >= 3 activate, and restricting to the favoured out_tok set trades recall for precision (F1 0.45, mass 0.73). No simple predicate explained which k occurrences stay silent.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=12: k, f, p, r; t=17: k, p, f; t=11: k, f, p) and the token being output (most: f, p, r, n, 1, z; least: w, g, t, y); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=7 & t=10.
